reason: While the conflict is indeed depicted as national (the Hebrew people against the Egyptian people), the statement's claim that it is NOT religious is inaccurate. The text fundamentally centers on religious issues: Moses and Aaron's core demand is 'שַׁלַּח אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י וְיָחֹ֥גּוּ לִ֖י בַּמִּדְבָּֽר' ('Let my people go, that they may hold a feast for me in the desert'). The conflict is explicitly about the right to worship God ('וְיַֽעַבְדֻנִי' - 'and they shall serve me'). God's agency is central throughout the narrative, and the plagues are divine acts to demonstrate God's power. The religious dimension is not merely present but is the fundamental basis of the entire conflict.
